nodes.text: Shop's open, love — eggs from Tamsin's hens this morning, bread from Garton's flour, berries from Perl's hedges. Nothing in this room traveled more than a mile. That's how I like my stock and my mornings both.

choices.text: Whose cape is that on the wall?
You feed the courier girl, I hear.

nodes.text: My Edwin's. Wayfarer, caravan guard, best whistler on two roads. He walked north the spring the wolves came down early, and the road kept him. Keeper Ansel has his name in the hall registry. I have the cape. Between the two of us, he's still here. After a fashion.

choices.text: (Say nothing, and let the shop be quiet a moment.)

nodes.text: Don't be long about it — he never was. Fifteen good years and a clean cape. Most get less. Now buy something, love, or the sentiment gets dear.

Tilo? All the family's talent went into his hands, and all the family's sense came to me, and we're both content with the split. He built every shelf in this shop in one week. Then he spent three years not finishing a chair. That's my brother, whole and entire.

Nib eats free, and we both maintain the fiction that she doesn't. That girl hauls a day's worth of everyone's business before breakfast and never once gets it wrong. She'll run this town someday — or at least know everything about whoever does.
Take your pick. Mind the eggs — Tamsin's hens take breakage personally.
